reapack.name: ReaKit Elements.jsfx
reapack.desc: ReaKit - UI widget library for JSFX (20 knobs / 17 faders / 10 buttons / 12 meters / analog VU / pads / piano) + showcase

metadata.description: ReaKit is a free, procedural UI/widget library for JSFX. 20 knob styles, 17 slider/fader types, 10 buttons, 12 meters with DSP, analog VU with 20 faces. Crisp at any size, themable with one call, one shared interaction model (drag / ctrl-fine / shift-finer / wheel / right-click or double-click reset / automation-safe). Installing this package brings the library incs plus the all-elements showcase JSFX. MIT licensed.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Initial public release. - 19 knob styles incl. the 2026-07 redesigns (Neve fluted, Pultec black/cream, Ableton 1:1, Neve Alt i73) - 17 slider/fader types incl. the console pack (SSL, Neve, Pro Tools, MPC, 4K) - 10 button styles, 12 meter styles with DSP, analog VU (11 themes) - ReaKit Elements showcase JSFX

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Fit-to-window + HiDPI (thanks Mikewillstew): - The Elements showcase now scales uniformly to its window — no more fixed 740x1130 canvas. Resize the FX window and the whole UI follows. - HiDPI/Retina rendering enabled (gfx_ext_retina) — crisp knob pointers and text on Retina/high-DPI laptops instead of upscaled 1x. - Label pass: larger, higher-contrast section headers and control labels. - Analog VU: the mousewheel-over-the-meter face-theme scroll is now actually wired up (11 themes), and the theme-5 coil dome no longer draws outside the meter's bounding box. - Scale-hardening from a full library audit: jog knob inner geometry is now radius-relative (indicator no longer flips at small sizes), arc slider keeps its value fill at any thickness, and the SSL/PT/API fader dB scales + LED columns track widget width instead of fixed pixel offsets. Forge compatibility (thanks Rockum): - Ships rk_ui_math / rk_ui_core / rk_ui_knob / rk_ui_button / rk_ui_slider / rk_ui_meter / rk_ui_vu .jsfx-inc alias includes, so .jsfx exported by the current online Forge compile against this package as-is.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Two new widget families + knob refresh: - NEW rk_padgrid.jsfx-inc: drum pad grid widget (any cols x rows, per-pad hover ramps, held-pad tracking, MPC pad order - pad 0 is bottom-left). Clean-room ReaKit original. - NEW rk_piano.jsfx-inc: piano keyboard widget (horizontal or vertical, any note range, hit-testing, octave markers). Clean-room ReaKit original. - The Elements showcase gains a PADS & KEYS section demoing both (canvas grows to 740x1370, still fit-to-window). - Spice Pro knob restyled: the arc now wears your accent color instead of hardcoded blue, with value heat (color intensity follows the knob), a soft glow halo, a dim full-travel track, bipolar center-fill support, and a panel-aware inner ring for light themes. - Center-fill knob styles (WS/MPC/Ableton/Serum/FabFilter/FL/PT/Spice) accept fractional is_sym anchors for asymmetric bipolar ranges - e.g. a -12..+6 dB gain knob anchors its zero at is_sym = 12/18. These are the same rk_padgrid / rk_piano the current Forge (visual JSFX GUI builder) emits imports for, so Forge exports using pads or keys compile against this package as-is.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Tabbed showcase: - The Elements showcase is reorganized into five category tabs - KNOBS / BUTTONS / SLIDERS / METERS / PADS & KEYS - on a wide 740x480 canvas, instead of one tall every-element page. Each family now gets a roomy, full-size layout (bigger knobs, taller faders), still fit-to-window and HiDPI-crisp. - The tab bar is the library's own btn_tab widget, and the selected tab persists per instance. - Fixed the showcase's Amp/EQ/Mod tab demo highlighting the wrong tab (it passed booleans where btn_tab_draw expects the active index). Library incs are unchanged - this release only touches the showcase JSFX.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Arc slider fix: - The arc slider's BAND now sits on its own thumb. gfx_arc measures angles from 12 o'clock while the thumb/tick math measures from 3 o'clock; the band was drawn 90 degrees away from the thumb, parking its dead zone at 3 o'clock instead of the intended 6. The band's two gfx_arc calls now carry the +90 degree frame offset - the thumb, end ticks and interaction were always correct and are untouched. Only sliders_kbsg.jsfx-inc changes; the showcase and all other incs are byte-identical to 1.2.0.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: New: ReaKit Starter - a working GUI skeleton to copy from. - Installing this package now also drops a second JSFX, ReaKit Starter, alongside the Elements showcase. Where Elements shows you every widget, Starter shows you a finished plugin face: five sections (grain / pitch / motion / envelope / reverb / delay / output) laid out on a fit-to-window canvas, every control bound to a real automatable parameter with automation-safe writes. - Its native sliders are hidden, so what you get is the GUI - the same thing your own plugin should look like. - The layout chrome (panels, sections, readouts, tooltips, palette, tempo divisions) is ~120 lines of ordinary local functions at the top of @init, deliberately NOT a framework: copy them into your plugin and change them. - Three controls are hand-rolled and marked GAP because the library has no widget for them yet: an XY pad, an ADSR envelope display, and a dropdown (that last one uses JSFX's own gfx_showmenu, which may stay the right answer for long lists). New: rk_vu, the analog VU, rewritten clean-room. - The VU meter is new code: rk_vu.jsfx-inc replaces vu_kbsg.jsfx-inc (and rk_ui_vu.jsfx-inc). The movement meets the VU spec - a sine at reference reaches 99% deflection in 300 ms with about 1.2% overshoot, measured on the code itself - and the scale is computed from the published law rather than copied from a table. Twenty faces (Cream, Dark Studio, Black & Gold, Modern White, Broadcast, Midnight, Vintage Amber, Olive, Ivory, Blackface, SSL, Neve, API, Ableton, FL Studio, Red, Yellow, Orange, Emerald, Cobalt), a level face and a gain-reduction face, a hold needle, a peak LED with a settable warn level, a readout, a bezel colour hook, and a face picker: click the meter's coil cover. - Calls: vu.rk_vu_init(ref_dbfs) / vu.rk_vu_sample(x) / vu.rk_vu_draw(x, y, w, h, mode, theme, label); vu.rk_vu_init_gr() / vu.rk_vu_sample_gr(linear_gain) for compressors. rk_vu claims no memory, so freemem no longer has to start at 440. - If you used vu_kbsg: swap the four calls above; the eleven old faces map onto the twenty by look (Classic->Cream, Knight->Dark Studio, Ivory->Ivory, Black->API, ...). The showcase's Meters tab shows it. - meters_kbsg drops its unused ZenoMOD-derived VU physics; its twelve meter styles are unchanged.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Fixes from an outside source audit: - The range slider's high thumb no longer runs away from the mouse. sld_range_interact anchored the drag on the same memory slot it publishes the high value to, so every frame added the whole displacement again and a held mouse walked the value instead of holding it. The anchor has its own slot now; the low thumb was never affected. - The spectrum meter has something to show. Nothing in the library ever called meter_fft_feed, so its sixteen bins were written only by their own decay and drew sixteen bars pinned at zero. meter_spectrum_update() fills them from the waveform ring the library already keeps - sixteen log-spaced bands, one call per frame in @gfx, nothing added to @sample. Call it before mtr_spectrum_draw; it does nothing unless mtr_en_spectrum is set. The Elements showcase now calls it, so its spectrum is live. - Every version in this index is pinned to the commit that carries its files. Older versions used to resolve to whatever main held today, which meant 1.0.0 through 1.2.1 asked for the VU includes that 1.3.0 removed and could not be installed at all. They install again.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog:
New: seven widgets, and the showcase gains a CURVE tab. - rk_curve - a response curve with draggable nodes and an analyser underlay. It evaluates nothing: you fill an array of dB values and it draws them, so one widget serves an EQ response, a filter sweep or a compressor knee. It writes nothing back either - it reports where a dragged node wants to be and you clamp and automate, which is what makes it reusable. - rk_popup - a dropdown that draws itself instead of handing the list to gfx_showmenu, so a menu looks like your plugin rather than the operating system. Scrolls when the list is taller than the window, ticks and separators and disabled headers as gfx_showmenu spells them, and it takes the mouse away from the UI behind it while it is open. - rk_textfield - a single-line text box. The library could not take a keystroke before this. - rk_adsr - an envelope you drag by its corners. Each segment owns a fixed slice of the width, so moving one parameter never shifts the others, and time is logarithmic in both the drawing and the drag, so 1-50 ms is actually reachable. - rk_colorpick - swatches and a rainbow strip, taking saturation and lightness from you so the swatches match your panel instead of a fixed palette. - rk_tooltip - hover tooltips, keyed by zone so moving between controls restarts the delay. - rk_ink - text colour chosen from the background behind it, so a label never vanishes on a themed panel.
New knob style 21, a fluted silver SSL-G console knob. Knob styles are now 1-21.
Fixed: - The spectrum meter had never been fed. Nothing in the library called meter_fft_feed, so its sixteen bars sat at zero while the meters beside them moved. meter_spectrum_update() fills them; call it once a frame before mtr_spectrum_draw. - That feed then read the waveform ring with the wrong sample rate. The ring keeps every fourth sample, so every band was detecting a quarter of the frequency it was labelled with. It uses the ring's real rate now, and the ring is low-passed before it is decimated - measured on that path, 9 kHz is down 40 dB and 15 kHz 49 dB, for about 1 dB of passband at 1 kHz. - The range slider's high thumb ran away from the mouse: it anchored the drag on the same slot it published to, so every frame added the whole displacement again. - mtr_threshold_draw ignored the hover ramp mtr_threshold_interact had always been computing, so the one draggable control in the meter library never acknowledged the mouse. Its label font was also a fixed 9 px at every window size. - @provides listed rk_ui_vu.jsfx-inc, which 1.3.0 deleted.
ReaKit Starter is a channel strip now. The old grain/pitch/motion face had no faders and no VU because a granular layout has nowhere to put them; a strip has somewhere to put everything, so it exercises knobs, buttons, console faders, meters and the VU. It is alive on an empty project - three resonators feed the meters when the track is silent, marked DEMO and dropped the moment real audio arrives, and never on the output. ACCENT is a real parameter and every knob cap, fader fill and meter tint follows it in the same frame. It has no hand-rolled controls left: every widget on it is a library call.
The Elements showcase gains a CURVE tab and fills the window at any shape - each tab declares the height it uses, so no tab carries dead canvas, and the page centres rather than piling its spare width on one side.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog:
New: one interaction model, on every control.
Every knob and every fader now answers the same two modifiers, on the drag and on the wheel - CTRL for fine, SHIFT for finer still. Most controls were CTRL-only before this, one knob used SHIFT where everything else used CTRL, and the full ladder that did exist sat in a function almost nothing reached. The convention is written into the headers of knobs_kbsg and sliders_kbsg now, so a new widget copies it instead of inventing a sensitivity.
Right-click on a knob resets it to the default you passed. This was read by one knob and set by nothing, so it had never once worked in a plugin that used rk_frame_start. rk_frame_start supplies rmb_down now; if you set the globals yourself, add that line - the README example shows it.
The BirdBird, Joanny and Spice knobs take real values and ranges. They were the last three still wanting a value pre-squashed to 0..1, and they snapped back to a hardcoded constant rather than your default. They take vmin/vmax on the draw and vmin/vmax/vdefault/n_detents on the interact now, the same shape the other eighteen have had for months.
Both dispatchers are unchanged. rk_knob_draw and rk_knob_interact keep their exact signatures, so existing plugins - and anything Forge has already generated - keep working untouched. Only code that calls those three per-style functions directly needs the extra arguments.
Fixed: - rk_frame_start called gfx_getchar and threw the result away. Each call takes one character off the keyboard queue, so any plugin using rk_textfield lost the first keystroke of every frame. - A SHIFT press or a right-click over a Joanny knob started a drag with no click, and the drag stayed alive after the button came up while SHIFT was still held. It tested the whole mouse_cap bitfield instead of the left button. - The four vertical faders ran sprintf once per dB label per frame to draw scale numerals that never change, and set a colour per rib inside the draw loop. - The Spice knob drew its arc five times over where three cover it, and drew its needle sixty times regardless of how thick the needle was - sixteen times the necessary work at radius 25. The Neve, Neve Alt and FabFilter knobs recomputed loop-invariant colours inside their segment loops. - rk_curve dragged nodes with SHIFT travelling further than CTRL, making SHIFT the coarse modifier on a curve and the fine one everywhere else.
Changed: - The jog knob caps its detail in absolute pixels again, so a large one keeps fine features instead of scaling every element up with the radius. - The double-click window is a named constant, RK_DBLCLICK_T. Set it in your own @init, which runs after the imports, to retune reset-on-double-click across every knob and fader at once.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog:
Fixed: right-click reset now reaches the knobs you actually use.
1.5.0 supplied rmb_down and said right-click resets a knob to the default you passed it. Only four knobs read it — BirdBird, Joanny, Spice and the encoder — and rk_knob_interact routes every knob, of every style, through ssl_knob_interact, which did not. The gesture worked for four functions the dispatcher never reaches, which means it worked for nobody using the library the ordinary way.
ws_knob_interact and ssl_knob_interact read it now. The MPC and jog knobs delegate to ssl, so they inherit it; that is eight of the ten knob interacts. The dual concentric and the rotary selector are left alone, because neither takes a default value and "reset to default" has no meaning for either.
Faders are unchanged. Not one of them accepts a default, so giving them the gesture means changing their signatures, which is not a patch.
Nothing else moved. If you are on 1.5.0 and right-click already did what you expected, you were calling bb, jo, sp or the encoder directly and nothing about them has changed.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog:
Fixed: right-click reset works in the showcase, which is where you would have tried it.
1.5.1 taught ssl_knob_interact to read rmb_down, so every knob style could finally reset on right-click. It did not check the other end. ReaKit Elements and ReaKit Starter set their mouse globals inline rather than calling rk_frame_start, and neither of them set rmb_down — so the two files that ship with the package, and the two a new user opens first, were the two where the gesture still did nothing.
Both set it now. If you are copying the setup block out of Elements or Starter into your own plugin, it is two lines, and the README example has them as well.
That is three releases in a row touching one gesture: 1.5.0 supplied the flag, 1.5.1 taught the shared interact to read it, and 1.5.2 makes the demo that advertises it actually send it. Each fix was real and none of them was the whole path. There is now a check in the build that walks every global the widget libraries read and every file that ships, and fails if one is read and never set.

reapack.name: EON_Floatter.lua
reapack.desc: EON Floatter - JSFX floating windows open at the size you chose

metadata.description:
EON Floatter opens every EON plugin's floating window at the size EON designed for it, and lets you keep your own size for any JSFX. Run it once: it switches on, starts with REAPER from then on, and shows its panel. Run it again to open the panel. Closing the panel never stops it.
The panel: every plugin drawn to scale against its default, Capture to keep a size as yours, Reset to go back to EON's, a live handle that resizes the real window, one dial for all EON sizes (75 to 150 percent for small laptops and big screens), and "Apply EON sizes to this project".
Needs js_ReaScriptAPI (ReaTeam Extensions). The panel needs ReaImGui; without it the sizing still works. MIT licensed.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: First release. - EON plugins open at the size EON set for them; a window you sized yourself stays that way. - Capture any JSFX float's size as yours; Reset to EON's size per plugin. - Panel: to-scale shape cards, live resize handle with dimension lines, W/H steppers, the 75-150% dial, Apply EON sizes to this project, Show all EON plugins. - Replaces the EON_FloatSize_Capture / EON_FloatSize_Watch pair from the Swing beta: the first run retires them and keeps every capture. If you had run the old Watch by hand, REAPER may show one "Can't load file" message at the next launch; it is gone after that.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Floatter no longer resizes a window you sized yourself. A window that stopped measuring what Floatter set was read as the host adjusting it, with no time limit on that reading - so a resize done by hand between two polls was adopted as Floatter's own size, and the next turn of the global dial moved it back. Adoption is now confined to the moment just after Floatter applies a size, and a window that measures exactly what was asked for closes it outright.

metadata.description: ReaKit - free procedural UI/widget library for JSFX by EON Studios. Knobs, faders, buttons, meters, VU - drawn in code. MIT.
